summary: The change makes the `stash` CLI pin every package it installs or recommends (@cipherstash/stack, the integration adapter, stash itself, and the one-shot @cipherstash/wizard run) to exact versions embedded at build time from sibling workspace manifests, and adds a version-skew check on already-installed packages that, interactively, offers to reinstall them at the embedded version. It touches no encryption, payload or key-handling code; the risk is release-train coherence. Because Changesets versions packages independently (`fixed: []`) and stash only peer-depends on @cipherstash/stack with a wide range, a sibling can release without a new stash release, leaving the published CLI pinning older versions. Init would then install the older release and, for projects already on the newer one, report it as skew and offer (default yes, bundled with any missing installs) to downgrade it. Pins also turn an unpublished train version (e.g. a partial publish) into a hard install failure where a bare install used to succeed. Unit, CLI E2E and a built-artifact embed check exist and the CI jobs passed, but none covers newer-than-expected installs or registry availability. Overall impact medium; focused review recommended.

behaviour_changes.description: `stash init` install-deps now runs package-manager installs with exact specs (`@cipherstash/stack@<v>`, adapter@<v>, `stash@<v>` as dev) taken from the build-time embed instead of bare names resolved via dist-tags. In source mode (no embed) it falls back to bare names.

New version-skew detection reads node_modules/<pkg>/package.json and flags any exact-string mismatch (older OR newer) against the embedded version. Interactively it adds the skewed packages to the single install confirm (initialValue true), so accepting also reinstalls existing packages at the embedded version; non-interactively it only warns and prints align commands.

tsup now reads stash, stack, stack-drizzle, stack-supabase, prisma-next and wizard package.json files at build time (via RELEASE_TRAIN_MANIFESTS) and defines __STASH_RUNTIME_VERSIONS__ in both bundles; a missing manifest/version fails the build, and a malformed embed throws at module load.

User/agent-facing guidance is pinned: requireStack hint in main.ts, missing-package hint, native-binary recovery hint (was `stash@latest`), install-eql manual note, and `.cipherstash/context.json` installCommand (stack only).
`stash wizard` one-shot spawn now runs `@cipherstash/wizard@<embedded version>` instead of the latest dist-tag.
Bundled skills (stash-cli, stash-drizzle, stash-dynamodb, stash-encryption, stash-supabase) document pinning and add a verify-what-resolved note; these ship into customer repositories.

failure_scenarios.title: Published CLI's pins go stale when a sibling releases alone; init installs, and offers to downgrade to, an older release
failure_scenarios.trigger: A release bumps @cipherstash/stack (or an adapter) without a `stash` changeset, e.g. stack 1.0.0-rc.2 ships while stash stays 1.0.0-rc.1; or a user runs an older cached `npx stash` against a project already on a newer release.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Versions are fixed into the CLI bundle at its build time (tsup.config.ts:33-58). Changesets versions packages independently (`fixed: []`) and stash only peer-depends on @cipherstash/stack with `>=1.0.0-rc.0` under onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange, and has no dependency at all on the adapters or wizard, so a sibling release does not force a stash release. The published stash then keeps pinning the previous versions. versionSkew compares exact strings (install-deps.ts:74), so a NEWER installed version is reported as skew; interactively the align specs are pushed into the same install command (install-deps.ts:216-221) behind a confirm whose default is yes (install-deps.ts:226).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Fresh `stash init` installs a release older than the current rc (the inverse of #661, now deterministic rather than dist-tag dependent), potentially reintroducing bugs fixed in the newer rc. A user who already upgraded and presses Enter (often because a missing adapter is being installed in the same prompt) has @cipherstash/stack/adapters downgraded. Recoverable by reinstalling, but silent unless the warning is read.

existing_verification.description: install-deps unit tests cover skew where the installed version is OLDER (0.19.0) than expected, accept/decline and non-interactive paths; CI 'Run Tests' jobs passed.

missing_verification: No test for an installed version NEWER than the embedded one (direction-aware skew).
No release-process check that stash is republished whenever a release-train sibling is published.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Make the release train coherent: add the train packages to a Changesets `fixed` group (or a CI check that a stash changeset accompanies any train-package changeset). In init, only offer alignment when the installed version is older, or make the align a separate confirm defaulting to No.

failure_scenarios.title: A pinned version that is not on npm turns init and `stash wizard` into hard install failures
failure_scenarios.trigger: A release-train manifest carries a version that was not (or not yet) published: a partially failed `changeset publish`, a package bumped but whose publish was rejected, or a train member not intended for publishing.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The embed takes whatever version is in the workspace manifest at build time (tsup.config.ts:33-41) regardless of registry state; release builds all packages then publishes them (package.json:34). Install and the wizard spawn now request exactly that version (install-deps.ts:221/253, wizard/index.ts:48), where the previous bare name would have resolved some published version.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Every `stash init` for that CLI version fails to install the affected package (ETARGET/404), leaving init reporting 'Still missing'; `stash wizard` fails to start when not locally installed. Loud, but publishing is irreversible so the fix is a new release.

existing_verification.description: release-train test asserts each train manifest exists and has a version (does not check publishability).

missing_verification: No check that every embedded version is published (or about to be published) before the CLI that pins it is published.
Whether @cipherstash/wizard@0.5.0-rc.1 and @cipherstash/prisma-next@0.4.0-rc.1 exist on npm could not be checked (no registry access).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Post-publish smoke step that runs `npm view <pkg>@<embedded version>` for each train entry; publish train siblings before stash; consider falling back to the bare spec with a warning on ETARGET.

failure_scenarios.title: Turbo build cache can reuse a CLI bundle with stale embedded adapter/wizard versions
failure_scenarios.trigger: A local or cached `turbo build` after only stack-drizzle, stack-supabase, prisma-next or wizard manifests changed, whose output is then published or tested.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The stash build task hashes `$TURBO_DEFAULT$` inputs of the CLI package plus upstream workspace deps (turbo.json:6); the adapters and wizard are not CLI dependencies, so changes to their package.json do not invalidate the CLI build, yet tsup reads them.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A CLI bundle pins outdated adapter/wizard versions without any build failure. The release workflow runs on a fresh GitHub runner with no cache restore configured, which reduces likelihood there.

existing_verification.description: runtime-versions-embed e2e test compares the built bundle to current manifests, which would detect a stale cached bundle where it runs (CI test job, not release.yml).

missing_verification: Release workflow does not run the embed check before `changeset publish`.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add the sibling manifests to the CLI build task's turbo `inputs` (or disable caching for the CLI build), and/or run the embed e2e check in release.yml before publishing.

verification_gaps.description: Skew handling is tested only for older-than-expected installs; behaviour when a project is ahead of the CLI's release (downgrade offer) is untested.
Nothing in the release process verifies that the CLI is republished with current pins when siblings release, or that pinned versions exist on npm.

recommended_controls.description: Review install-deps.ts:175-226: whether aligning existing installs should share the missing-install confirm with default Yes, and whether newer installed versions should be treated as skew at all.
Put release-train packages in a Changesets `fixed` group or add a CI rule requiring a `stash` changeset whenever a train package has one, so the published CLI's pins track sibling releases.
Add a unit test for installed-newer-than-expected and a post-publish smoke check (`npm view` per embedded pin) in release.yml.
Include sibling manifests in the CLI build's turbo inputs and run the embed e2e check before publish.
